choice.ex: (A) acknowledges (B) desirable (C) discover 근거 ❶❷❸❹ 해설: (A) ❶ science’s embrace of ignorance(무지의 수용) + ❷ 확인 없이 안다고 가정하는 것이 최악 = 모른다는 사실을 인정 / (B) ❸ a valuable rather than a questionable attribute = 바람직한 특성 / (C) ❹ simply out of curiosity to see what will happen = 무슨 일이 일어나는지 발견. conceals는 ❶ embrace와 정반대, suspicious는 ❸에서 ‘벗어난’ 과거의 시각(questionable), dictate(좌우하다)는 결과를 모른 채 ‘보기 위해’ 한다는 ❹와 모순. 요약문 해석: 과학은 자신이 모든 것을 알지는 못한다는 사실을 (A) 인정하며, 그것이 결과를 검증하지 않고 가정하는 것이 심각한 실수인 이유이다. 호기심은 이 제 (B) 바람직한 특성으로 여겨지고, 실험이 항상 공식적인 계획을 필요로 하는 것은 아니다. 실험은 단지 무슨 일이 일어나는지 (C) 발견하기 위해 실행될 수 있 다.
choice.psg: ❶ Experiments testify to science’s embrace of ignorance. ❷ Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. ❸ The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. ❹ For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology (“state your hypothesis and then test it”), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, “One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen.” ❺ Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin’s son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. ❻ You never know until you try.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) convincingly (B) incorporated (C) encompass 근거 ❶❺❻❽ 해설: (A) ❶ a better way of explaining the evidence = 증거를 더 설득력 있게 설명 / (B) ❺ 뉴턴 이론의 성과는 무시될 수 없었고 아인슈타인 이론은 그 것을 똑같이 잘 설명함 = 받아들여 포함 / (C) ❽ match all the successes of Einstein’s theory = 아인슈타인의 성과를 포괄. narrowly는 ❻ broader와 반대, dismissed는 뒤의 rather than overlooking them과 모순(❺ could not be ignored), overturn은 ❽ 성과에 필적해야 한다는 조건과 반대. 요약문 해석: 과학자들은 잘 뒷받침된 이론을 단지 그 예측 몇 개가 틀렸다는 이유로 제쳐 두지 않는다. 경쟁 이론이 증거를 더 (A) 설득력 있게 설명할 수 있을 때에만 그렇게 한다. 아인슈타인의 상대성 이론은 뉴턴 이론의 성공들을 간과하지 않고 (B) 받아들여 포함했기 때문에 인정을 얻었으며, 앞으로의 어떤 후속 이 론도 마찬가지로 더 멀리 나아가면서 아인슈타인의 성과를 (C) 포괄해야 할 것이다.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) eliminated — (B) design — (C) halts

choice.ex: (A) preserved (B) luck (C) drives 근거 ❹❺❼ 해설: (A) ❹ will tend to be perpetuated = 보존 / (B) ❺ it is a matter of chance = 운 / (C) ❼ Through endless repetition of this cycle … organisms evolve = 진화를 이끎. eliminated는 ❹(영속됨)와 반대, design(의도·설계)은 ❺의 chance와 반대, halts(멈추게 하다)는 ❼ organisms evolve와 반대. 요약문 해석: 세포가 분열할 때, 작은 복제 오류들이 종종 그 유전체에 슬며시 끼어든다. 세포의 전망을 개선하는 오류는 (A) 보존되는 경향이 있고, 돕지도 해치 지도 않는 오류는 (B) 운에 따라 살아남거나 사라지며, 심각하게 해로운 오류는 그것을 지닌 세포와 함께 사라진다. 끝없이 반복되는 이러한 변이의 선별이 진화 를 (C) 이끄는 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. ❷ On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell’s prospects. ❸ But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. ❹ Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. ❺ Changes due to mistakes of the second type ― neutral changes ― may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. ❻ But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. ❼ Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.

Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶❷ / ❸❹❺ / ❻❼ / ❽❾❿) · ❸ ‘Gargle again’은 ❷의 첫 헹굼(Then, gargle with water) 뒤에 와야 함 · ❻ ‘Your taste pattern’은 ❶~❺ 실험과 ❺ 친구들과의 반응 비교 결과를 받음 · ❽ ‘For example’은 ❼ 미각자 유형과 행동 장애의 연관성에 대한 예시
order.A: Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends’.
order.B: For example, “non-tasters” tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, “super-tasters” may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.
order.C: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results.
order.D: Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶ / ❷❸ / ❹ / ❺❻) · ❷ ‘suppose they know ~ without bothering to check’는 ❶ ‘embrace of ignorance’(무지의 수용)의 반대 사례로 ❶을 부연 · ❹ ‘experimental science today’와 ‘out of curiosity’는 ❸ 실험 철학의 ‘등장(과거)’·‘호기심의 해방’을 이어받음 · ❺ ‘Indeed ~ one should do’는 ❹ ‘One can conduct an experiment’를 한층 강화(할 수 있다 → 해야 한다)
order.A: For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology (“state your hypothesis and then test it”), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, “One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen.”
order.B: Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute.
order.C: Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin’s son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. You never know until you try.
order.D: Experiments testify to science’s embrace of ignorance.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶❷❸ / ❹❺ / ❻❼ / ❽) · ❹ 'These discrepancies'는 ❸의 '예측이 관찰과 일치하지 않는 경우들'을 받음 · ❻ 'It did'는 ❺의 'explain these successes equally well'을 받음(아인슈타인 이론이 실제로 그렇게 했다) · ❽ 'any new theory'는 ❼ '아인슈타인을 넘어설 중력 이론'을 받아 그 인정 조건을 제시
order.A: It did, and that is why we now view Einstein’s theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton’s theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein’s.
order.B: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton’s theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations.
order.C: These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. read.ko: 그래서 비록 미각이 시각, 청각, 또는 심지어 촉각만큼 화려하지는 않지만, 적어도 여러분의 입안에서는, 화학 작용이 운명이 될 수 있기 때문에 여러분이 그것에 좀 더 세심한 주의를 기울이는 것이 타당하다.
read.en: So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.

read.ko: 실험들은 과학의 무지에 대한 수용을 증명한다.
read.en: Experiments testify to science’s embrace of ignorance.

read.ko: 거의 틀림없이 과학자가 할 수 있는 가장 최악의 것은 그들이 확인하려는 수고를 들이지 않고 주어진 시나리오에서 일어날 일을 그들이 안다고 가정하는 것이다.
read.en: Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check.

read.ko: 실험 철학의 등장은 의심스러운 특성이 아닌 가치 있는 특성으로서의 호기심의 해방과 동시에 일어났다.
read.en: The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute.

read.ko: 오늘날의 실험 과학은 철학적 틀과 승인된 방법론(‘가설을 세우고 나서 그것을 검증하라’)에 의해 뒷받침되고 있다고 종종 여겨지지만, 사실은 과학 철학자 Ian Hacking이 말하듯이, ‘누군가는 무슨 일이 일어날 것인지를 알아보기 위해 그저 호기심에서 실험을 수행할 수도 있다’.
read.en: For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology (“state your hypothesis and then test it”), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, “One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen.”

read.ko: 게다가 Charles Darwin의 아들인 천문학자 George Darwin의 관점에서는 비록 그것이 효과 없는 것으로 증명될 가능성이 대단히 크더라도 가끔 누군가는 완 전히 무모한 실험을 해야 한다.
read.en: Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin’s son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless.

read.ko: 여러분은 여러분이 시도하기 전까지는 절대 알 수 없다.
read.en: You never know until you try.

read.ko: 단지 우리가 그것을 뒷받침하는 증거를 설명하는 더 나은 방법이 있을 때에만 우리는 과학 이론을 버리거나 대신할 수 있다.
read.en: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it.

read.ko: 뉴턴과 아인슈타인의 이론들이 훌륭한 예시들을 제공한다.
read.en: The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples.

read.ko: 방대한 양의 증거가 뉴턴의 중력 이론을 뒷받침해 주지만, 19세기 후반에 이르러 과학자들은 그것의 예측들이 관찰 결과와 완벽하게 일치하지 않는 경우들을 발 견하기 시작했다.
read.en: A vast body of evidence supports Newton’s theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations.

read.ko: 이러한 불일치들은 아인슈타인이 자신의 일반 상대성 이론을 전개했을 때 비로소 설명될 수 있었고, 그것은 관찰 결과와 일치할 수 있었다.
read.en: These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations.

read.ko: 그럼에도 불구하고, 뉴턴의 이론의 많은 성과는 무시될 수 없었고, 아인슈타인의 이론이 만약 이러한 성과를 똑같이 잘 설명할 수 없었다면 인정을 받지 못했을 것이다.
read.en: Still, the many successes of Newton’s theory could not be ignored, and Einstein’s theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well.

read.ko: 그것은 그렇게 했고, 그것이 우리가 오늘날 아인슈타인의 이론을 뉴턴의 이론보다 더 포괄적인 중력 이론으로 보는 이유이다.
read.en: It did, and that is why we now view Einstein’s theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton’s theory.

read.ko: 오늘날 몇몇의 과학자들은 아인슈타인의 이론을 넘어설 중력 이론을 찾고 있다.
read.en: Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein’s.

read.ko: 만약 어떤 새로운 이론이 언젠가 인정을 받는다면, 그것은 아인슈타인의 이론이 작동하지 않는 새로운 영역에서 작동할 뿐만 아니라 아인슈타인의 이론의 모든 성과에 필적해야 할 것이다.
read.en: If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein’s theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein’s theory does not.

read.ko: 바쁜 하루의 중간에 잠시 멈춰서, 정신을 새롭게 하고 에너지를 재충전하는 순간을 가지는 것을 상상해 보라.
read.en: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy.

read.ko: 이러한 한낮의 휴식의 힘은 종종 과소평가된다.
read.en: This power of a midday break is often underestimated.

read.ko: 여러분이 특히 여러분의 두뇌를 자극하도록 설계된 활동들을 가지고 일상에서 벗어날 때 여러분은 인지적 피로를 예방하고 남은 하루 동안의 생산성을 높인다.
read.en: When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day.

read.ko: 간단하지만 효과적인 뉴로빅 운동이 그러한 휴식 시간에 꼭 알맞다.
read.en: Neurobic exercises ― simple yet effective ― are perfect for such breaks.

read.ko: 그것들은 여러분의 뇌의 다른 영역들을 겨냥하여, 그것을 기민하고 민첩하게 유지한다.
read.en: They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert.

read.ko: 이러한 운동들은 오후의 힘든 일들을 위해 여러분을 기운 나게 하고 준비시켜 주는 정신적 오아시스를 만들어 준다.
read.en: These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon’s challenges.

read.ko: 이 전략적인 멈춤은 단순한 휴식이 아니며, 그것은 여러분의 인지 능력을 증대시키고 여러분의 정신이 또렷하고 집중된 상태가 유지되도록 보장해 준다.
read.en: This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused.

read.ko: 짧게 뉴로빅 운동들을 시도하는 것만으로도 점심시간 동안 여러분의 인지 상태에 기적 같은 효과를 낳을 수 있다.
read.en: Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch.

read.ko: 글쓰기 또는 식사와 같은 일상적인 과업들을 위해 여러분의 주되지 않은 손을 사용하는 것으로 시작하라.
read.en: Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating.

read.ko: 이 간단한 전환이 여러분의 뇌를 자극하여, 전형적으로 사용되지 않는 경로들을 활성화시키고 사고에서의 더 큰 유연성을 촉진시킨다.
read.en: This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren’t typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.

read.ko: 세포가 분열할 때, 그것의 두 딸세포들의 유전체들은 종종 서로 간에도, 또는 모세포의 그것과도 완전히 일치하지는 않는다.
read.en: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell.

read.ko: 드물게 그 오류가 더 나은 것으로의 변화를 나타낼 수도 있지만, 더 높은 확률로 그것은 세포의 전망에 큰 차이를 일으키지 않을 것이다.
read.en: On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell’s prospects.

read.ko: 그러나 어떤 경우에는 그 오류가 심각한 손상을 초래할 것이다. 예를 들어 핵심 단백질의 코딩 서열을 망가뜨림으로써 그렇게 할 것이다.
read.en: But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein.

read.ko: 첫 번째 유형의 실수로 인한 변화들은 영속되는 경향이 있을 것인데, 변화가 일어난 세포가 스스로를 복제할 높아진 가능성을 가지고 있기 때문이다.
read.en: Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself.

read.ko: 두 번째 유형의 실수로 인한 변화들, 즉, ‘중립적인’ 변화들은 영속될 수도 있고 아닐 수도 있다. 변화가 일어난 세포나 그것의 사촌들이 성공할지는 운의 문제이 다.
read.en: Changes due to mistakes of the second type ― neutral changes ― may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed.

read.ko: 그러나 심각한 손상을 초래하는 변화들은 어느 곳에도 닿지 못한다. 그것들을 겪는 세포는 죽고, 자손을 남기지 않기 때문이다.
read.en: But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny.

read.ko: 이러한 ‘돌연변이’와 ‘자연 선택’의 순환의 끊임없는 반복을 통해 유기체들은 진화한다. 그들의 유전적 특성들은 변화해서, 유기체에게 환경을 더 효과적으로 활 용하고, 다른 것들과의 경쟁 속에서 살아남으며, 그리고 성공적으로 번식할 수 있는 새로운 길들을 때로는 제공한다.
read.en: Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.

para.en: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends’. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders. For example, “non-tasters” tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, “super-tasters” may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.

Experiments testify to science’s embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology (“state your hypothesis and then test it”), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, “One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen.” Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin’s son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. You never know until you try.

We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton’s theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton’s theory could not be ignored, and Einstein’s theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein’s theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton’s theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein’s. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein’s theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein’s theory does not.

Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day. Neurobic exercises ― simple yet effective ― are perfect for such breaks. They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert. These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon’s challenges. This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused. Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren’t typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.

When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell’s prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type ― neutral changes ― may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
